newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya central bank buys dlrs to stem shilling rise.
newsitem.headline: Kenya central bank buys dlrs to stem shilling rise.

text.p: The Kenyan shilling was unchanged against the dollar on Wednesday after the central bank bought dollars to stem a shilling rise, commercial bank dealers said.

The Central Bank of Kenya posted the shilling at a mean rate of 54.93 against the dollar unchanged from Tuesday. Against the pound, the shilling was posted at a mean rate of 88.28 from 87.97 on Tuesday.
Dealers said the central bank bought dollars on Tuesday in the market from tea and coffee sales and foreign investors.
"If we had dumped the dollars into the market, the shilling would definitely have appreciated," one dealer said.
Dealers said the bank appeared to support the dollar at the current level which was why the market had been quiet for the last three weeks.
Last week a central bank official said the shilling was threatening to strengthen but he reiterated the central bank would leave the determination of the exchange rate to market forces.
Dealers said a stronger shilling could hurt exporters while a stable unit reflected a stable economy and was good for long- term investment ahead of general elections expected late this year.
"What they (the central bank) really don't want to see are huge or sudden fluctuations in the exchange rate," a dealer said. "Whatever the direction, they'd rather a gradual movement."
The money market was unchanged with overnight rates quoted at 10 to 15 percent.
